title: Multi-language SDK: streaming + tool-calling + structured schema examples
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Scope: Define and deliver a consistent SDK surface for streaming responses, tool/function calling flow, and typed structured outputs across TypeScript, Python, and Go. Deliverables: API signatures, short idiomatic examples for each language, compatibility layer notes for older SDK users, tests and one cross-language example app. Goal is to make streaming+tools+structured outputs feel native in each language while preserving parity with the hosted API behavior and Console debug metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Public SDKs (TS/Py/Go) expose a streaming API that returns incremental tokens/events and a final parsed structured object when applicable.
Tool/function calling flow is supported end-to-end: tool discovery metadata, tool invocation event stream, and tool response injection into the model context.

Structured output support: SDK includes typed helpers (interfaces/classes) and runtime validators that map to a recommended JSON schema pattern; examples must show both strict parsing and lenient fallback.
Compatibility: documented upgrade path for existing users using legacy stream APIs; compatibility shim included in TS SDK to emulate previous callback style.
Test coverage: unit tests for parsing partial streams, tool-calling error paths, and schema validation; an integration example (mini chat app) in the repo that works in CI for all three languages.
technical_notes: Design decisions: prefer push-based streaming (async iterator/event emitter) for TS/Py and channel-based streaming for Go. Structured outputs use recommended pattern: top-level `schema_version`, `structured_payload` plus `raw_text` fallback. Tool calling should be represented as an event sub-type (e.g., STREAM_EVENT_TOOL_CALL / STREAM_EVENT_TOOL_RESULT) so consumers can subscribe only to tool events. SDKs must attach metadata for Console tracing (request_id, model_variant, backend_node) in stream start events.
examples: Compatibility shim example (TS): `client.chat.streamCompat(...)` that accepts old signature (onToken, onComplete) and internally maps to new event stream. This shim logs a deprecation warning and will be removed in 6 months.

2026-03-03 - Dana Kim (API): Reviewed schema proposal. Requested explicit `schema_version` field in stream start and done events for future migration. Added to technical notes.

2026-03-09 - Nirav Patel (QA): Wrote test plan for partial stream reassembly and tool failure injection scenarios. Found an edge case: tool-call followed by immediate done event with no tool_result event. We will emit an empty tool_result with `status: 'skipped'` in that case.
